name: Manor
description: The basic fief for game purposes: the land (around six hundred acres) traditionally required to maintain a knight, his family and household retainers, yielding about twenty pounds a year.

name: Fief
description: Land or another valuable right loaned by a lord to a vassal in exchange for military support, counsel and other benefits.

name: Commendation Ceremony
description: The ritual solemnizing the lord-vassal relationship, with oaths before mortal witnesses and God, typically including homage and an oath of fealty.

name: Homage
description: Act in the commendation ceremony in which the kneeling vassal-to-be places his joined hands within the lord's hands and asks to become his vassal.

name: Oath of Fealty
description: Brief oath sworn by a new vassal on a Bible or relic promising the liege aid in war, good counsel and whatever else is customary.

name: Knighthood
description: Ceremony creating a knight, often tied to vassalage since a knight usually joins the liege's household as a minor vassal.

name: Scutage
description: A fine paid in lieu of knight service, costing up to three pounds per year.

name: Mesnie
description: A lord's household body of knights, costing about five pounds a year each to maintain.

name: Subinfeudation
description: The process by which tenants-in-chief divide estates into smaller parcels to support warriors, forming a pyramid of power down to the individual knight.

name: Tenants-in-Chief
description: Powerful families holding land directly from the king of England in exchange for military service, forming England's upper nobility.

name: Norman Invasion
description: The Norman Conquest of England in 1066, since which all English land has been owned by the king.

name: England
description: Kingdom with the simplest feudal system, where all land is owned by the king; the peasantry model used in this book.

name: Domesday Book
description: Record that lists English manors, including one manor that had no inhabitants.

name: Demesne
description: Land reserved for the lord's own use, farmed on his behalf by villeins as part of their rent; usually the most fertile land of the manor.

name: Acre
description: Historical measure of land a person with an ox can plow in a day, treated as 4,840 square yards; relevant to Terram magic targeting.

name: Hide
description: Amount of land (120-144 acres) required to maintain a family of affluent free peasants, producing four pounds for a lord.

name: Virgate
description: Land a two-ox team could plow in a day, a quarter or sixth of a hide (24-32 acres), sufficient to support an unfree peasant family.

name: Virgater
description: Peasant who rents a virgate of land; worth about a pound a year to a lord.

name: Bovate
description: Land half the size of a virgate, used to supplement the income of families with other primary work.

name: Bovater
description: Peasant renting a bovate, often a miller, reeve, shepherd or manor servant.

name: Cottar
description: Peasant with ten acres or less, living by hired labor or a trade, such as a blacksmith; half of manorial peasant families.

name: Village
description: Settlement where villeins live, averaging around sixty families; becomes a town only through a charter granting legal rights.

name: Town
description: Settlement granted rights by an overlord in a charter, whose residents are free of villein service; an average town has perhaps three hundred people.

name: City
description: A settlement where a cathedral is.

name: Large-field Farming
description: Farming system using about half of Mythic Europe's agricultural land, suited only to heavy soils, found in central England and near large French and German cities.

name: Farming (Renting)
description: Period English term for renting out land or manors, convenient for the Order of Hermes since paying for land use is not against the Code; falling from favor in 1220.

name: Order of Hermes
description: The order of magi, for whom renting land is convenient; its oldest covenants predate the manorial system and are thus allods.

name: Code of Hermes
description: The Order's law, which does not forbid paying for land use.

name: Mythic Europe
description: The game setting, whose economy is essentially agricultural and whose manorial system is failing.

name: Capital Messuage
description: The lord's enclosed piece of land around his house, containing his hall, outbuildings and curtilage.

name: Hall
description: The chief building of a manor and residence of the lord or his bailiff, typically a timber long house 60-75 feet long.

name: Bailiff
description: Appointed deputy who lives in the hall when the lord does not, keeps order in the manor court and cares for the famuli.

name: Steward
description: Lord's officer who convenes the manor court and sees to the lord's rights.

name: Foundation Charm
description: Charm placed in a hall's walls or foundations to protect the building, set by a hedge witch or via traditional sacrifice; may anchor a faerie guardian spirit.

name: Witch Bottle
description: Foundation charm that hexes minor magic users entering a building; can detect cursing power and the Gift and carries a PeCo effect up to level 40.

name: Hedge Witch
description: Minor magic user who can place foundation charms (see Hedge Magic).

name: Hedge Magic
description: Supplement whose rules can simulate witch bottles and hedge witches.

name: The Gift
description: Magical potential that witch bottles can detect, letting magi identify young Gifted people as potential apprentices.

name: Hermetic Magic
description: Magic of the Order of Hermes, which easily resists the weak hexes of witch bottles.

name: Intellego
description: Technique used in the witch bottle detection effects (InVi).

name: Vim
description: Form used in witch bottle detection effects (InVi) for the curse power and the Gift.

name: Perdo
description: Technique of the witch bottle's harmful effect (PeCo).

name: Corpus
description: Form of the witch bottle's harmful body effect (PeCo).

name: Terram
description: Form of magic affecting dirt; an acre to two feet deep is an Individual target with three size modifiers.

name: Penetration
description: Measure of a magical effect's ability to overcome resistance, listed for witch bottle effects.

name: Castles in Lieu of Halls
description: On large estates a castle may replace the hall; castles are detailed in Covenants and summarized in Chapter Eight: Massed Combat.

name: Covenants (supplement)
description: Supplement describing castles in detail.

name: Dovecote
description: Small building housing several hundred doves or pigeons that tenants may not harm; attracts familiars and magical animals.

name: Pinfold
description: Pen within a messuage for impounded stray animals, which become the lord's property.

name: Curtilage
description: Unroofed land enclosed within the messuage's wall, used for orchards or holding court.

name: Stackyard
description: Robustly fenced area in the messuage where harvested grain is stacked before threshing.

name: Steedles
description: Small pillars raising granaries or grain stacks to prevent rodent infestation.

name: Granary
description: Building storing threshed grain and flour; a prime raider target.

name: Scarecrow
description: Straw manikin invented in a story seed after a plague; faeries are drawn to them and they can take on faerie roles, even forming armies.

name: Faerie
description: Faerie powers and creatures, drawn to scarecrows and folk practices, dwelling in the wasteland and playing with natural measures.

name: Infernal
description: Realm whose servants take crow shape and whose minor demons flee intense masses.

name: Dominion
description: Divine influence spread by clearing faerie wasteland and boosted by marathons of masses.

name: Divine
description: Realm protecting hallowed places such as churchyards.

name: Magic Aura
description: Aura that powerful magical creatures must stay within, which can be suppressed by intense masses.

name: Familiar
description: Magical animals bonded to magi; dovecotes attract carnivorous familiars and potential familiars.

name: Allod
description: Land held outright without feudal relationship; the oldest Hermetic covenants predate the manorial system and so are allods.

name: Glebe
description: Farmland reserved for the maintenance of the Church and its servants, tilled by or rented out by the priest.

name: Arable
description: The most precious land, used to grow grain and legumes.

name: Meadow
description: Land used for growing grass harvested as hay, which limits herd size over winter.

name: Pasture
description: Grazing land, primarily for sheep, often marginal land at the edge of the waste.

name: Waste
description: Unplanted land, including woods and marshes; the domain of the faeries.

name: Foldcourse
description: A piece of land over which the right to graze sheep has been granted.

name: Pannage
description: Right, paid for by villeins, to turn pigs loose in the woods.

name: Famuli
description: The lord's liveried household staff, lodged and fed by him, including laborers, shepherd, swineherd and dairymaid.

name: Market Fair
description: Fair held on the lord's demesne where surplus is exchanged for manufactured goods, typically twice a year.

name: City & Guild
description: Supplement covering towns, fairs, trade and businesses.

name: Quern
description: Hand mill for grinding grain, illegal in some places because lords demand use of their mill.

name: Multure
description: Fee of a proportion of the grain milled, paid by millers renting mills.

name: Commons
description: Village areas, typically pasture called the village green, set aside for villeins and regulated by the manor court.

name: Tragedy of the Commons
description: Later idea popularized by the Enclosure Movement that commons are destroyed by overuse, which the book says does not apply because greens are regulated.

name: Enclosure Movement
description: Post-game-period English movement that popularized the tragedy-of-the-commons idea and gave greens to landed gentry.

name: Turbary
description: The right to cut peat.

name: Forest
description: Royal hunting land; in England much woodland is royal forest inspected by a forest warden.

name: Forest Warden
description: Royal officer inspecting the king's woodland and fining overgathering and illegal clearances.

name: King John
description: King of England who was excommunicated and later swore fealty to the pope; Devon and Cornwall paid him to be deforested.

name: Devon
description: English county whose people paid King John 2,200 marks and 20 palfreys to be deforested.

name: Cornwall
description: English county whose people paid King John 5,000 marks to be deforested.

name: Parks and Lodges
description: Portions of wasteland reserved by lords for pleasure and as game reserves.

name: Right of Warren
description: Lord's right to trap and raise small game, extending to pests and even magical monsters and vis sources.

name: Vis
description: Raw magical power; vis sources may belong to lords under warren, and a bishop may seek to tithe it.

name: Mineral Rights
description: Rights to resources beneath the ground, held by the lord or king.

name: Manor Court
description: Court dealing with lesser matters like assault, minor thefts and disputes between villeins, convened by the steward.

name: Manorial Rolls
description: Long records of previous cases and debts kept by the court clerk.

name: Heriot
description: Death duty owed when a household head dies, often the peasant's best beast.

name: Mortuary
description: Fine of the second-best beast collected at death to make good tithes assumed withheld, easing passage through Purgatory.

name: Laity Objects
description: Items given as gifts to the Church by dying people, such as the deathbed or best robe.

name: Purgatory
description: Afterlife state through which a peasant who paid mortuary has easier passage.

name: Tallage
description: Lord's right to levy any amount of money from his villeins at any time, proportional to their holdings.

name: Gite
description: French tax consisting of a feast for the lord and retinue on his tour of inspection; sometimes sold to others.

name: Royal Courts
description: Courts dealing with the king's rights and crimes punishable by death, such as murder and arson.

name: Church Courts
description: Courts dealing with priests and crimes against God or the Church.

name: Jury of Inquisition
description: Group appointed by the court to investigate a matter and report at the next session.

name: Beadle
description: Villein officer, also called messor, acting as the reeve's enforcer, summoning people to court and collecting fines.

name: Natural Measures
description: Measures based on the body or nature, such as salmon 'as thick as a man's wrist', which generally favor the lord.

name: Tiny Eggs
description: Story seed in which a faerie makes every egg on a manor thimble-sized, disrupting dues and prompting witchcraft accusations.

name: Weight in Gold
description: Story seed where an abbot promised a mercenary captain his weight in gold and seeks magi to feed him magically created food.

name: Daniel
description: Biblical figure who fixed a weigh-in with the help of God, whose miracle the abbot hopes to repeat.

name: Warped Consors
description: Story seed about highly Warped covenfolk from a fallen Autumn covenant causing strife with nobility and church.

name: Warping
description: Magical distortion leaving covenfolk highly Warped, such as a man with a hand five times normal size.

name: Autumn Covenant
description: A covenant in its declining season; one in a neighboring Tribunal has fallen in a story seed.

name: Spring Covenant
description: A young covenant, the setting for the Swift Assarting story seed.

name: Tribunal
description: Hermetic regional body and court; the king of England may demand payment for fines levied at Tribunal.

name: Seizure
description: The automatic passing of a felon's goods to his lord.

name: Fines for the King
description: Story seed where the king of England claims reparation when magi in England are fined by Tribunals.

name: House Tytalus
description: Hermetic House whose domus magna floats off the coast of Normandy, suspected of arranging the king's intervention.

name: Domus Magna of House Tytalus
description: Tytalus headquarters that floats smugly off the coast of Normandy and causes strife in neighboring Tribunals.

name: Normandy
description: Region where, like England, farmland must be held from the king.

name: Merchet
description: Fine paid to a lord for permission for serfs to marry, widely loathed by peasants.

name: Leywrite
description: Theoretical adultery tax charged on a woman who made herself unmarriageable by losing her virginity.

name: Childwrite
description: Tax on unmarried pregnancy, often absorbed into leywrite.

name: Tithe of Vis
description: Story seed in which a bishop's representative inspects a covenant to tithe its vis, books and magic items.

name: Fines for Being Fined
description: Rule that a peasant fined outside the manor court owes his lord equivalent compensation since the money was the lord's.

name: Curate
description: Local priest appointed by the bishop to care for souls in a parish; temporary curates serve perpetual curates.

name: Rector
description: Whoever has the right to collect a parish's tithes.

name: Churchyard
description: Hallowed place protected by the Divine where villagers gather, drink, dance and hold informal markets.

name: Hearth Mate
description: A curate's domestic woman-of-all-work, effectively often a wife.

name: Brotherhood of the Black Mask
description: League of annoyed minor English nobles that robs and beats Italian priests given livings; a social movement without a leader.

name: Swift Assarting
description: Story seed about brigands claiming to be former assarting workers of a covenant that actually assarted magically.

name: Assarting
description: Carving new cropland or meadow from fertile wasteland; can be done magically, alarming nearby lords.

name: Conquest
description: Taking land by force, rare among lower nobility except in anarchy or civil war.

name: Alms Land
description: Land given to the Church in perpetuity, still held from a major noble who keeps rights like knight service.

name: Charities
description: Lands given to the Church in exchange for services such as masses for the donor; increasingly offered to nunneries.

name: Royal Charter
description: Charter by which a town holds directly from the king, placing it beyond the agricultural aristocracy.

name: Catching Up On Masses
description: Story seed where priests perform a marathon of backlogged masses, boosting the Dominion and disturbing faeries and demons.

name: Benedictine Monks
description: Monks following the Benedictine model whose wilderness monasteries created allodial Church land.

name: The Church
description: The greatest landholder in Mythic Europe, portrayed as oppressive by modern standards and supportive of serfdom.

name: House Merinita
description: Hermetic House with a weaker focus on combat.

name: House Jerbiton
description: Hermetic House with a weaker focus on combat.

name: House Criamon
description: Hermetic House with a weaker focus on combat.

name: Manticore
description: Mechanical manticores ridden by undead knights, cited as a fantastic covenant option.

name: Grog
description: Covenant servant-soldier characters whose backgrounds can draw on peasant material.

name: Companion
description: Non-magus player characters whose backgrounds can draw on peasant material.

name: Magus
description: Hermetic wizard; magi prefer static laboratories and may identify Gifted apprentices.

name: Serf
description: Unfree agricultural worker whose labor is owned by his lord in exchange for land; owes rent, week works and boon works.

name: Week Works
description: Serf labor obligation expressed as days per week, each measured from sunrise to noon.

name: Boon Works
description: Added days of labor theoretically performed out of love for the lord, who feeds laborers.

name: Censum
description: Annual fee excusing a peasant from week work for a year, sometimes used as a punishment.

name: Ministeriales
description: Villein knights in German duchies who pay for their keep with military service.

name: Reeve
description: Villein officer overseeing daily work, usually appointed on Michaelmas; lucrative but unpopular and prone to corruption.

name: Michaelmas
description: Feast on 29 September, just after harvest, when reeves are usually appointed.

name: Hayward
description: Villein officer overseeing harvest laborers, guarding the crop and the pasture.

name: Woodward
description: Lesser office caring for the lord's plantations.

name: Forester
description: Lesser office caring for the lord's hunting wood.

name: Ale-taster
description: Officer, often a woman, ensuring ale brewed on the manor is fit for sale.

name: East Anglia
description: Region where peasants maintain dykes and lords of marshy manors run large sheep flocks.

name: The Wandering Poor
description: Story seed about strangers who may be saints, God, demons or faeries in disguise.

name: Famuli Matters
description: Story seeds giving a below-stairs view of servants, such as cleaning up after crises.

name: Half-free Peasant
description: Free person who rents villein land and so owes villein service.

name: Free Peasant
description: Agricultural worker who owes no service to the lord for land, under ten percent of most manors' population.

name: Church-scot
description: Small fee many free peasants owe the Church each November.

name: Demon
description: Infernal beings that walk the roads bringing temptation and leave their haunts during marathons of masses.

name: Joining the Navy
description: Story seed where a nobleman demands ship carriage from a port town near a covenant.
